newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-PAPIN DOUBLE SINKS LEADERS MONACO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PAPIN DOUBLE SINKS LEADERS MONACO.

text.p: Jean-Pierre Papin scored twice in 12 minutes to give Bordeaux a 2-1 home win over title-chasing Monaco in the French first division on Wednesday.

Monaco, who lost 3-1 away to Internazionale of Italy in the UEFA Cup in their previous match, remain 11 points clear of second-placed Paris St Germain, who were held 1-1 at Bastia on Tuesday, with five matches to go.

Papin, who had not scored since March 9, completed his second double of the season in the 50th and 62nd minutes to lift Bordeaux one place to fifth. Belgium captain Enzo Scifo pulled one back for Monaco with an injury-time penalty.
The former France captain put Bordeaux in front from a counter attack when he raced onto a through ball from the right from Ibrahim Ba to steer it past goalkeeper Fabien Barthez.
Papin evaded two tackles before putting the ball under Barthez for the second.
"That does you good to rediscover these sensations," said Papin, who took his league tally to 12.
"I've been doing what I know for a long time and today it was all smiles. This is revenge for our bad luck because I think we played a great match in Paris on Saturday without reward."
Bordeaux lost the League Cup final to Strasbourg on penalties at the Parc des Princes on Saturday.
Monaco coach Jean Tigana said: "We have a few days to recover and prepare for the Inter match (UEFA Cup semifinal second leg on Tuesday)."

Nantes extended their unbeaten run to 26 league games with a 1-0 win at Strasbourg thanks to a 74th-minute goal from Christophe Le Roux and climbed to third one point above Bastia. Strasbourg dropped to sixth.
Defending champions Auxerre, seventh, revived their hopes of a place in Europe next season with a 2-0 win over Le Havre with goals by captain Franck Silvestre and Algeria's Moussa Saib.
Lyon striker Alain Caveglia was shown the red card in the 25th minute for bringing down Romanian Corneliu Papura, who scored Rennes' opening goal, from behind. Rennes won 2-1.
In the 65th minute, Rennes defender Mickael Silvestre was dismissed for a second bookable offence.
Marseille striker Xavier Gravelaine made up for a penalty miss with an 89th-minute equaliser in a 2-2 draw at home against Montpellier.
Gravelaine, awarded the penalty after being fouled by veteran keeper Bruno Martini, could have equalised in the 66th minute but put his spot kick wide.
Midfielder Franck Rizzetto put Montpellier ahead with a fine shot just before halftime.

Defender Hamada Jambay equalised three minutes after the interval with a spectacular 30-metre volley, but less than two minutes later Ibrahim Bakayoko headed Montpellier back into the lead after Rizzetto lobbed German goalkeeper Andreas Koepke.
Montpellier, who meet Guingamp in a French Cup semifinal on Saturday, are unbeaten in 20 matches in all competitions, 13 in the league.
Guingamp's preparation to face Montpellier was less happy as they went down 2-0 at Metz.
Bottom team Nice, who meet second division Laval in the other semifinal on Sunday, had another nail hammered into their relegation coffin at home when Lens came from behind to win 2-1.

Lens went some way toward easing their relegation worries when midfielder Mickael Debeve hit an 82nd-minute winner. Czech Republic winger Vladimir Smicer equalised following Mohamed Chaouch's early goal for Nice.
